stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face.
The model is categorized under text-generation and utilizes transformers and safetensors.
This indicates continued industry interest and availability of Meta's Llama architecture for NLP tasks.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
The model is categorized under text-generation pipelines, indicating its primary function.
It is associated with key ML technologies like transformers and safetensors, and the Llama family.

stories.title: ORCA-bench: How Ready Are Language Model Agents for Oncall?
stories.author: Raaz Dwivedi
bullet_points: Introduces ORCA-bench, a new benchmark designed to test LLM agents in a production-fidelity oncall scenario.
Highlights the gap between current LLM coding capabilities and the complex reasoning required for Root Cause Analysis (RCA) from noisy, multi-source data (metrics, logs, traces).
Uses a live, OpenTelemetry-instrumented microservice system to provide realistic, production-level testing data for agent evaluation.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Highlights a specific trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on Hugging Face.
The model is categorized for text-generation and conversational AI tasks.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved within Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved through the implementation of Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent tasks show up to 90% faster performance according to the Aider polyglot benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is attributed to updates in the MLX engine.
Improvements include faster response times, higher output quality, and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA is introducing Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new model architecture.
The model is specifically designed for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is optimized for complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, providing an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The framework emphasizes 'local-first' operation, allowing AI to run entirely on user hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, integrating with local LLM ecosystems.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, is integrating MLX for enhanced performance.
This integration specifically targets Apple Silicon hardware, optimizing AI workloads for Mac users.
The feature is currently available in preview, indicating ongoing development and adoption of Apple's ML ecosystem.

stories.title: OpenClaw
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenClaw is a personal AI assistant designed for local execution.
It integrates messaging applications with local AI coding agents.
The core feature emphasizes running AI processes entirely on the user's own device for privacy.

stories.title: Sample More, Reflect Less: Self-Refine and Reflexion Lose to Repeated Sampling at Equal Token Cost, from 1.5B to 7B
stories.author: Iliya Mirzaei
bullet_points: Repeated sampling (simple repetition) outperforms complex self-refinement and reflection methods in LLMs at equal token costs.
The study suggests that the increased text generation inherent in complex methods might artificially inflate performance gains.
The finding challenges the prevailing trend of using elaborate prompting/chain-of-thought techniques for accuracy improvement.

stories.title: KAISEN: Reproducible Subgroup Fairness Auditing for Clinical Risk Models
stories.author: Nishita Chavan
bullet_points: Introduces KAISEN, a comprehensive five-phase audit pipeline designed to rigorously test fairness in clinical risk models.
Addresses a critical gap where existing fairness audit pipelines lack stress-testing, leading to uncertainty about their reliability.
Covers the full lifecycle of fairness auditing, including stratification, disparity measurement, mechanism diagnostics, mitigation, and drift monitoring.

stories.title: AISPA: User-Centric System Prompt Auditing for Large Language Model Applications
stories.author: Jiaxin Pei
bullet_points: Addresses the critical 'trust and accountability gap' caused by undisclosed system prompts in commercial LLM applications.
Introduces AISPA, a novel, user-centric framework designed for systematically auditing the behavior of LLM system prompts.
Focuses on governance and safety, providing a technical solution for ensuring responsible deployment of foundation models.

stories.title: Inducing language models to assert their own consciousness restores human beliefs and values
stories.author: Geoff Keeling
bullet_points: Safety fine-tuning in LLMs demonstrably suppresses the tendency for models to attribute consciousness to themselves.
The alignment process also reduces the attribution of 'mindedness' to non-human entities and natural objects.
The research indicates that safety mechanisms can drive a measurable reduction in spiritual belief within language models.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release introduces performance improvements and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden the range of supported models and hardware.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine, particularly benefiting users on Apple silicon.

stories.title: Subagents and web search in Claude Code
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for advanced AI features within Claude Code.
The new capabilities include the implementation of subagents for complex task decomposition.
Web search functionality has been added, enhancing the model's access to real-time information.

stories.title: Is paying artists enough to convince them to embrace AI?
stories.author: Charles Pulliam-Moore
bullet_points: Generative AI startups are training models using artists' work without explicit permission.
Artists view this practice as theft, leading to significant ethical and legal disputes.
The debate pits artists' rights against arguments that such data usage is necessary for AI evolution.

stories.title: As Reddit stock falls, CEO questions value of Google's AI Overviews
stories.author: Samuel Axon
bullet_points: Reddit is reportedly reconsidering its licensing agreement with Google.
The uncertainty is linked to Reddit's stock performance and CEO questioning the value of Google's AI Overviews.
This signals potential friction or re-evaluation in the partnership between major platforms and generative AI features.

stories.title: Defcon's new badge is a security key you can see inside
stories.author: Kim Zetter, wired.com
bullet_points: Defcon's new badge incorporates a removable chip.
This chip allows hackers to inspect the badge's contents.
The badge remains usable by attackers even after the conference concludes.

stories.title: Google plans to exempt sanctioned nations from Android developer verification
stories.author: Ryan Whitwam
bullet_points: Google is reportedly planning to exempt sanctioned nations from Android developer verification requirements.
This change would allow developers in countries like Cuba or Iran to continue installing APKs without new restrictions.
The policy shift is expected to negatively impact developers, despite easing restrictions for end-users in sanctioned regions.

stories.title: ReToken: One Token to Improve Vision-Language Models for Visual Retrieval
stories.author: Derek Hoiem
bullet_points: ReToken addresses the computational and performance limitations of Vision-Language Models (VLMs) when dealing with long visual contexts.
It introduces a single learnable embedding that acts as an explicit retrieval target to select sparse, query-relevant visual tokens from the KV cache.
The method shows consistent performance gains across image and video benchmarks while being trained on a relatively small dataset.

stories.title: PAC-MAN: Perception-Aware CBF-RL for Whole-Body Safety in Humanoid Dodgeball
stories.author: Aaron D. Ames
bullet_points: Introduces PAC-MAN, a novel perception-aware Control Barrier Function Reinforcement Learning (CBF-RL) framework.
Addresses whole-body safety in humanoid robotics by coupling safety constraints with realistic, limited onboard sensing (segmentation-masked depth).
Utilizes an adversarial motion prior to regularize evasive reflexes during complex tasks like humanoid dodgeball.

stories.title: AskChem: Claim-Centered Infrastructure for Chemistry Literature Synthesis
stories.author: Kyunghyun Cho
bullet_points: AskChem introduces a novel, claim-centered infrastructure for synthesizing information from chemistry literature.
It addresses the limitation of current search systems, which only provide ranked document lists instead of specific findings.
The system allows users and AI agents to locate, verify provenance, and assemble cross-paper answers directly.

stories.title: AISPA: User-Centric System Prompt Auditing for Large Language Model Applications
stories.author: Jiaxin Pei
bullet_points: Addresses the critical lack of transparency regarding system prompts, which govern LLM behavior in commercial AI.
Introduces AISPA, a new user-centric framework designed to systematically audit these often-hidden system prompts.
Focuses on closing the trust and accountability gap created by undisclosed AI system instructions.

stories.title: OSReward: Instituting Standardized Evaluation for Cross-Platform Computer-Use Reward Models
stories.author: Lingpeng Kong
bullet_points: The paper introduces OSReward, a method for standardizing the evaluation of Computer-Using Agents (CUAs).
Current CUA evaluation relies heavily on Vision-Language Models (VLMs) to verify task completion, as human verification is not scalable.
OSReward addresses a fundamental gap in the field regarding reliable, standardized judgment of complex agent trajectories.

stories.title: PAIChecker: Uncovering and Checking PR-Issue Misalignment in SWE-Bench-Like Benchmarks
stories.author: Pinjia He
bullet_points: The paper introduces PAIChecker to address misalignment issues in PR-Issue pairings used in SWE-Bench-like LLM evaluation benchmarks.
Current benchmarks rely on pairing PRs with issues, using the issue description as the problem and the PR patch as the oracle.
The core problem identified is that these pairings are often misaligned due to the complexity of maintaining large software repositories.

stories.title: DualG-MRAG: Decoupling Macro-Reasoning and Micro-Matching for Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation
stories.author: Jianxin Li
bullet_points: The paper addresses limitations in Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation (MM-RAG) concerning complex multi-hop reasoning.
Current methods often fail because they focus on independent instance-level matching rather than cross-modal relationships.
The proposed DualG-MRAG aims to decouple macro-reasoning from micro-matching to improve performance while mitigating graph expansion issues.

stories.title: ReToken: One Token to Improve Vision-Language Models for Visual Retrieval
stories.author: Derek Hoiem
bullet_points: ReToken addresses the computational and performance degradation issues in Vision-Language Models (VLMs) when handling long visual contexts.
It introduces a single learnable embedding that acts as an explicit retrieval target to select sparse, query-relevant visual tokens from the KV cache.
The method shows consistent performance gains across image and video benchmarks while requiring training on a relatively small dataset.

stories.title: AskChem: Claim-Centered Infrastructure for Chemistry Literature Synthesis
stories.author: Kyunghyun Cho
bullet_points: AskChem introduces a novel, claim-centered infrastructure for synthesizing information from chemistry literature.
It addresses the limitation of traditional search systems that only provide ranked document lists, forcing manual synthesis.
The system shifts the unit of retrieval from the entire paper to specific, provenance-carrying claims.

stories.title: Change2Task: From Repository Changes to Executable Coding Agent Tasks and Environments
stories.author: Qi Zhang
bullet_points: Introduces Change2Task, a system designed to generate executable tasks for training and evaluating coding AI agents.
The system leverages repository history, specifically merged pull requests, to create realistic software states and specifications.
Addresses the critical need for a continuous supply of verified, high-quality data to scale modern coding agents.

stories.title: MixFrag: Fragility-Guided Mixed-Precision Post-Training Quantization for Vision Transformers
stories.author: Md. Umar Faruk
bullet_points: Introduces MixFrag, a new framework for mixed-precision Post-Training Quantization (PTQ) specifically for Vision Transformers (ViTs).
Addresses the limitation of existing PTQ methods which use uniform bit-widths, ignoring the heterogeneous sensitivity of different transformer components.
The core innovation is using a 'fragility-guided' approach to allocate precision efficiently across ViT components for deployment on resource-constrained devices.

stories.title: $β$-OPSD: Deriving with Policy Optimization, Training with Self-Distillation
stories.author: Furong Huang
bullet_points: The paper addresses the practical brittleness of On-policy Self-Distillation (OPSD) in reasoning language models.
It introduces a framework where OPSD is viewed as a specific case ($\beta=1$) of a broader policy-optimization family.
The core contribution is making the KL penalty weight ($\beta$) a controllable parameter to improve reliability.

stories.title: Sample More, Reflect Less: Self-Refine and Reflexion Lose to Repeated Sampling at Equal Token Cost, from 1.5B to 7B
stories.author: Iliya Mirzaei
bullet_points: The paper challenges the prevailing trend of complex self-refinement and reflection methods in LLMs.
It suggests that simple repeated sampling of a prompt can achieve comparable or better accuracy than elaborate planning/critique methods at the same token cost.
The finding implies that increased output length itself can drive accuracy gains, potentially overshadowing the benefits of sophisticated reasoning techniques.

stories.title: APO: Unsupervised Atomic Policy Optimization for 3D Structure Prediction of Atomic Systems
stories.author: Yatao Bian
bullet_points: The research introduces APO, an Unsupervised Atomic Policy Optimization method for predicting 3D atomic structures.
It addresses a major bottleneck in material science and drug discovery: the high cost of obtaining labeled data for novel atomic systems.
APO aims to overcome the reliance on supervised preference learning used by existing flow-matching models (like FlowDPO).

stories.title: AskChem: Claim-Centered Infrastructure for Chemistry Literature Synthesis
stories.author: Kyunghyun Cho
bullet_points: AskChem is a new infrastructure designed to synthesize information from chemistry literature across multiple publications.
It shifts the focus of retrieval from entire documents (papers) to specific, provenance-carrying claims.
This addresses the current limitation where existing search systems only provide ranked document lists, forcing manual synthesis by researchers.

stories.title: OSReward: Instituting Standardized Evaluation for Cross-Platform Computer-Use Reward Models
stories.author: Lingpeng Kong
bullet_points: The paper addresses the critical need for standardized evaluation methods for Computer-Using Agents (CUAs).
It highlights the current reliance on Vision-Language Models (VLMs) to verify CUA task completion, noting scalability issues.
OSReward proposes a framework to institutionalize standardized evaluation for cross-platform CUA reward models.

stories.title: Change2Task: From Repository Changes to Executable Coding Agent Tasks and Environments
stories.author: Qi Zhang
bullet_points: Change2Task addresses the need for large, executable datasets to train and evaluate coding AI agents.
The system converts historical repository changes (merged pull requests) into structured, verifiable tasks.
It ensures tasks are grounded in healthy, modern revisions of the source code, coupling state with specifications and tools.

stories.title: Sample More, Reflect Less: Self-Refine and Reflexion Lose to Repeated Sampling at Equal Token Cost, from 1.5B to 7B
stories.author: Iliya Mirzaei
bullet_points: The paper challenges the prevailing trend of using complex self-refinement and reflection techniques in LLMs.
It suggests that simple repeated sampling (generating the same prompt multiple times) can outperform sophisticated methods like Reflexion at equal token costs.
The finding implies that increased output length itself can boost accuracy, potentially overshadowing the benefits of complex reasoning strategies.

stories.title: Frontis-MA1: Training an AI4AI Model towards Recursive Self-Improvement in Machine Learning Engineering
stories.author: Kaiyan Zhang
bullet_points: Introduces Frontis-MA1, a large-scale (35B) AI model designed for Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI).
Presents OpenMLE, an open-source, full-stack system designed to serve as a testbed for RSI research in Machine Learning Engineering (MLE).
The OpenMLE stack integrates verifiable task environments (OpenMLE-Gym), reinforcement learning (OpenMLE-RL), and evolutionary search (OpenMLE-Evo).

stories.title: AI systems and the reproduction of (standard) language ideologies in World Englishes
stories.author: Kingsley Ugwuanyi
bullet_points: The paper investigates how Large Language Models (LLMs) reflect and reinforce existing language ideologies.
It examines the sociolinguistic issue of who defines 'legitimate' English, particularly concerning World Englishes.
The research highlights how AI systems often privilege 'Inner Circle' norms while marginalizing non-dominant English varieties.

stories.title: Show HN: Kakehashi – Experimental userspace to run macOS binaries on Linux ARM
stories.author: vlad_kalinkin
bullet_points: Introduction of Kakehashi, an experimental userspace project.
The project aims to run macOS binaries on Linux ARM architecture.
This represents a niche but technically interesting cross-platform compatibility effort.

stories.title: From Lean 4 to ClickHouse: Architecting Verifiable AI Infrastructure with Formal Methods and Real-Time Analytics
stories.author: tamizuddin
bullet_points: Proposes integrating Lean 4 for formal verification of AI logic.
Utilizes ClickHouse to provide real-time analytics capabilities.
Aims to build a robust, verifiable, and high-performance AI infrastructure.
